Grade: Grade 3
Subject: ENGLISH ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.4: Comprehension

SECTION 1: WELCOME

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: COMPREHENSION
Subject: ENGLISH ACTIVITIES · Grade: Grade 3
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Comprehension helps you succeed in ENGLISH ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: COMPREHENSION
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Construct sentences on have been demonstrated by

What this means
In this part you learn to construct sentences on have been demonstrated by. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: construct sentences on have been demonstrated by.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Comprehension”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can construct sentences on have been demonstrated by. Write or say your answer clearly.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Comprehension”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: construct sentences on have been demonstrated by)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Comprehension to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: construct sentences on have been demonstrated by.
3. Practise this skill: recognise the correct use  Learners construct 271 of subject-verb sentences using singular agreement to form and plural subjects for appropriate sentences, things at home and around.
4. Practise this skill: identify indefinite oral sentences using indefinite ( 6 lessons) pronouns in pronouns in pairs and in groups. communication about .
5. Make one local Kenya example of Comprehension from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Comprehension: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 3 learner study Comprehension?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

1. Know what Comprehension means in your own words.

3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
